newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish govt body approves TPSA telecoms sale plan.
newsitem.headline: Polish govt body approves TPSA telecoms sale plan.

text.p: The Polish government's economic committee (KERM) approved on Monday the sale plan of the country's telecommunications monopolist Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the government's press office said.
It said in a statement the KERM recommended the privatisation should be done in several stages, the first of which should take place in 1998.

"The method of privatisation should incorporate the sale of TPSA shares to domestic and foreign investors in a public offer and the sale of a stake to a strategic investor in the next stages of the process," the statement said.
It said that part of the money from the sale should be earmarked for important social goals, notably the reform of the social security system, but gave no figures.

The KERM asked the treasury and telecoms ministers to work out by the end of June a programme of TPSA privatisation which would include the size of the public offer in the first stage of the process, its structure and sale method.

The plan would also include privatisation costs, the use of money from the sale, the size of a potential additional share issue and an estimate of the impact the public offer combined with a new issue would have on the domestic capital market.
The KERM recommended that the ministers should consider introducing a TPSA share subscription for all its clients to "broaden the social effects of a public offer."
The KERM also decided that the telecoms minister would have to open up long-distance calls to other operators by January 1 1999. The statement gave no further details.
